fields.summary: The Board uses a sole source exemption (a legal exception to public bidding) to buy 52,920 antigen rapid COVID-19 test kits from Office Depot, LLC at $21.99 per kit, under an agreement effective January 6, 2022. The cost may not exceed $1,163,710.80 for the 2021-2022 school year. This is the first of two separate orders from the same vendor; the second is for another 52,920 kits at a different price.

The Board uses a sole source exemption (a legal exception to public bidding) to buy 52,920 antigen rapid COVID-19 test kits from Office Depot, LLC at $19.49 per kit, under an agreement effective January 10, 2022. The cost may not exceed $1,031,410.80 for the 2021-2022 school year. This is the second of two separate orders from the same vendor; the first is for another 52,920 kits at a different price.

The district and Peralta Community College District sign a memorandum of understanding (a formal partnership agreement) to run the Gateway to College Alternative High School at Laney College from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2023. The district pays Peralta, which invoices twice a year based on student attendance. The $652,465.95 cap is the projected 2021-22 cost, based on about 82 students.

22-0572.sourceIssue: The text states an amount not to exceed $652,465.95 but does not say whether the District pays Peralta Community College District or receives the money.

fields.headline: Accepts up to $30,000 from Alameda County Office of Education to launch an arts learning design team
fields.summary: The district and the Alameda County Office of Education sign a memorandum of understanding (a formal partnership agreement) to start an Arts Learning District Design Team to increase arts learning in the district. The county office pays the district up to $30,000, and the district invoices it for costs incurred. It runs from March 23, 2022 to June 30, 2022.

22-0574.note: Corrected: the agreement shows the Alameda County Office of Education pays the district, so this is revenue to the district, not an expense.
22-0574.sourceIssue: The text states an amount not to exceed $30,000.00 but does not say whether the District pays the Alameda County Office of Education or receives the money.
